subject: paediatrics
title: Breast Milk Jaundice, Crigler-Najjar and Biliary Atresia

steps.tx: Prolonged unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a thriving, healthy breastfed newborn defines **benign breast milk jaundice**. Developing after the first week of life, serum bilirubin levels peak between ten and fifteen days and persist for three to twelve weeks. The condition is mediated by high concentrations of beta-glucuronidase and non-esterified fatty acids in maternal milk, which hydrolyze conjugated bilirubin and enhance intestinal deconjugation.
steps.say: Breast milk jaundice persists for weeks in thriving infants due to increased enterohepatic deconjugation.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of bilirubin entering the gut, being deconjugated by beta-glucuronidase, and returning to the liver as unconjugated bilirubin.
vis.caption: Enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin, with intestinal beta-glucuronidase deconjugating bilirubin glucuronide for reabsorption. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Clinicians must differentiate breast milk jaundice from **early breastfeeding jaundice**. Breastfeeding jaundice develops during the initial two to four days of life as a direct consequence of inadequate caloric intake, dehydration, and infrequent nursing. Reduced enteral volume delays meconium passage, promoting substantial enterohepatic recirculation of bilirubin that resolves once lactation is properly established.
steps.say: Breastfeeding jaundice occurs early from inadequate milk intake and dehydration, improving with feeding support.

rows: Day 5 to 7, peaks at 2 to 3 weeks
Beta-glucuronidase in milk, high enterohepatic uptake
Healthy, vigorous suck, normal weight gain
Increase nursing frequency to 10 to 12 daily

steps.tx: The absolute therapeutic rule in breast milk jaundice is that **breastfeeding must not be discontinued**. Temporary cessation or substitution with artificial formula is unnecessary, undermines maternal lactation confidence, and risks premature weaning. In rare instances where total serum bilirubin approaches phototherapy thresholds, brief continuation of phototherapy alongside uninterrupted breastfeeding is completely safe.
steps.say: Breastfeeding should never be stopped for breast milk jaundice; maternal reassurance is the cornerstone.

left.title: Recommended Management
points: Reassure parents regarding benign natural course

right.title: Harmful Outdated Practices
points: Boiling breast milk to denature enzymes

steps.tx: A rare autosomal recessive inborn error of bilirubin clearance is **Crigler-Najjar syndrome type one**, caused by complete absence of hepatic uridine diphosphate glucuronosyltransferase enzyme activity. Serum unconjugated bilirubin rises catastrophically to twenty to forty-five milligrams per deciliter within days of birth, precipitating fatal kernicterus unless continuous sixteen-hour phototherapy and definitive orthotopic liver transplantation are provided.
steps.say: Crigler-Najjar type one represents total absence of glucuronosyltransferase, demanding liver transplantation.

steps.tx: Any infant presenting with jaundice persisting beyond fourteen days in term or twenty-one days in preterm neonates requires mandatory evaluation for **pathological neonatal cholestasis**. Defined by a conjugated direct bilirubin exceeding 1.0 milligram per deciliter, it signals hepatobiliary dysfunction. Characteristic physical signs include pale clay-coloured acholic stools, dark amber urine, and progressive firm hepatomegaly.
steps.say: Conjugated bilirubin exceeding one milligram per deciliter defines neonatal cholestasis and demands urgent evaluation.

left.title: Cholestatic Clinical Triad
points: Dark amber urine that stains nappies yellow

steps.tx: The most common surgical etiology of neonatal cholestasis is **extrahepatic biliary atresia**, characterized by progressive fibro-inflammatory obliteration of the extrahepatic bile ducts. Infants are typically born at term with normal initial birth weights, developing progressive jaundice, acholic stools, and hepatosplenomegaly at two to six weeks of age as bile flow completely ceases.
steps.say: Biliary atresia is progressive fibro-obliteration of bile ducts presenting with acholic stools and cholestasis.

rows: Good hepatic uptake, zero excretion into bowel
Confirms complete biliary obstruction at 24 hours
Bile ductular proliferation, portal fibrosis, plugs

steps.tx: Ultrasonographic identification of a triangular or tubular echogenic fibrous band anterior to the portal vein bifurcation constitutes the **triangular cord sign**. Measuring greater than four millimeters in thickness, it represents the obliterated extrahepatic bile duct remnant. Combined with a small, contracted, or absent gallbladder after fasting, it provides high diagnostic specificity for biliary atresia.
steps.say: The triangular cord sign on ultrasound identifies the fibrotic duct remnant in biliary atresia.

right.title: Differentiation from Hepatitis
points: Excretion into bowel on 24-hour HIDA scan
Giant cell transformation on liver histology

steps.tx: The primary surgical intervention of choice is the **Kasai portoenterostomy procedure**, performed by resecting the fibrous biliary remnant at the porta hepatis and anastomosing a Roux-en-Y jejunal loop directly to the exposed transected microductules. Crucially, surgical success directly depends on age at intervention, with biliary drainage achieved in eighty percent if operated before sixty days.
steps.say: Kasai portoenterostomy restores bile flow, with surgical success highest when performed before sixty days.

rows: Over 50 percent reach adolescence without transplant
Most develop progressive secondary biliary cirrhosis
Early progression to liver failure, mandates transplant
